questions.cardText:
[Archaeology] What is Senet, an artifact frequently discovered in ancient Egyptian burial sites?
A. A musical instrument
B. A medical device
C. A game
Answer: C. Senet is considered the oldest board game in human history, dating to 2500–3100 BCE. Relatedly, the Royal Game of Ur, discovered in present-day Iraq, is also considered one of the oldest known board games, dating back to around 2600 BCE.
questions.de: Was für ein Gegenstand ist Senet, das häufig in altägyptischen Gräbern gefunden wird?
questions.en: What kind of object is Senet, frequently found in ancient Egyptian burials?

timeline.labelEn: Earliest possible Senet boards, found in First Dynasty burials in Egypt
timeline.labelDe: Früheste mögliche Senet-Bretter aus Gräbern der 1. Dynastie in Ägypten

questions.notes: First Dynasty fragments (c. 3100 BCE) are only possibly Senet; the first unequivocal depiction is in the Third Dynasty tomb of Hesy-Ra.

questions.cardText:
[Engineering and Inventions] What was the first video game ever made?
A. Pong
B. Space Invaders
C. Tennis for Two
Answer: C. Tennis for Two, created in 1958, is considered the first video game ever made.
questions.de: Welches auf einem Oszilloskop gespielte Spiel des Physikers William Higinbotham von 1958 wird oft als erstes Videospiel bezeichnet?
questions.en: What 1958 game by physicist William Higinbotham, played on an oscilloscope, is often called the first video game?

timeline.labelEn: Tennis for Two is first shown at Brookhaven National Laboratory's visitors' day
timeline.labelDe: Tennis for Two wird erstmals beim Besuchertag des Brookhaven National Laboratory gezeigt

questions.notes: The card's 'first video game ever made' is contested: Wikipedia says only 'under some definitions' — earlier computer games such as OXO (1952) exist; Tennis for Two was the first made purely for entertainment.
